result.killer: PM_定期 (Produce Media): a dedicated tool for 12条 reports. It covers 特定建築物定期調査, 建築設備定期検査 and 防火設備定期検査, works on a tablet in the field, and outputs each 特定行政庁's forms (47 prefectures plus 13 cities), with yearly form updates. FireNET also produces 防火設備定期検査 reports. Lift reports are normally filed by the maintenance firm for the owner, and in Tokyo a lift association (東京都昇降機安全協議会) handles intake and pre-checks.
result.reason: The first check found no dedicated product. A non-government search did find one. PM_定期 makes 12条 reports for 特定建築物, 建築設備 and 防火設備 in every 特定行政庁's format and updates the forms each year. FireNET covers 防火設備. Lifts, the remaining category, are usually filed by maintenance firms for owners, and some prefectures have association filing services (宮崎). Cities post reminders and offer free Excel kits and e-filing. Owners don't fill in reports themselves; qualified inspectors must do it, which leaves only a thin reminder-calendar niche for small owners. PM_定期's pricing and customer numbers weren't found, and I didn't check whether it covers the 2025-07 form revision. Score 2.

The リスク評価書 is a one-off, free MLIT/全日 template under a request with no penalty; no commercial product was found for it.
result.reason: The recurring part, 取引時確認記録 plus the STR check, is already sold to 宅建業者. GOGEN's レリーズ本人確認 creates 本人確認記録 automatically, and since 2026-05-15 it also includes the RETPC STR checklist, with completion tracking. The release suggests describing that workflow in the risk report's 対応方針 section. Digital Garage's Musubellスマート本人確認 (2026-05-28) says it does eKYC, 反社 checks and auto-generated, stored records ahead of the April 2027 rule change; I saw that only in search summaries. TRUSTDOCK runs inside PICKFORM. What is left is the リスク評価書: a free MLIT and 全日 template, done once, under a request with no stated penalty. No commercial tool or writing service found. The market is large (133,727 firms in March 2026), but the uncovered job is thin.

coverage.found: 墓埋法施行規則 requires a 使用者 ledger kept by the cemetery manager. Cemetery operation needs a permit and is normally municipal or religious. Software found is municipal (Mitsubishi ぼさんシステム, and LGWAN tenders from Kurume, Matsue and Odawara) plus one funeral-company catalogue. No temple-specific package was found. coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: The amended 貨物自動車運送事業法 (promulgated 2025-06) adds a 5-year permit renewal, 適正原価 enforcement and 白トラ shipper liability. Parts took effect 2026-04-01 (shipper liability, subcontracting limit of 2). Renewal and 適正原価 duties come later, within 3 years of promulgation per an MLIT chart cited in search. The exact first renewal dates were not confirmed (the article fetch had no dates; the MLIT PDF was unreadable). 貸切バス: the 乗務記録 duty already exists; fares were revised in 2025-09. K09, K25 and K26 already cover logbooks and taxi. Candidate C15.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Street vendors: 露店 and 臨時 food permits are municipal with tiered fees. Kitchen-car permits became valid across the whole prefecture after 2021-06 in many prefectures, which removes the multi-permit pain. No management app found. Candidate C16 (weak). Money changers: not reached.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Childminders and unlicensed nurseries: 届出 within 1 month; annual 運営状況報告 (Setagaya 2025 deadline 10/31, e-filing available); penalty up to ¥500k; attachments include qualification, training and insurance copies. 2026 こども誰でも通園 adds a participation channel. Small food producers: HACCP plus 営業届出; pickle makers became permit-required in 2021; no 2026 rule change found. Tattoo and hunting outfitters: not reached.

result.competitor: I found no dedicated Japanese commercial product in vendor searches for 定期報告/防火設備/昇降機 report software (whether any exists was not fully checked). Partial substitutes: Kyoto city's free 入力支援ファイル (an Excel kit that prints the 防火設備 report); municipal Word/Excel forms; municipal e-filing portals (せんだいオンライン申請サービス, 千葉市電子申請, e-KOBE, Nagoya, Toyama; Tokyo electronic intake since 2024); and generic inspection photo apps (Asahi Sogo's インスペクションマネージャー). I assume, without checking, that inspectors and lift maintenance firms already handle reporting for owners.
result.duty: 建築基準法 s.12(1) and (3): owners or managers of designated buildings, building equipment, 防火設備 and lifts must have a qualified person (一級/二級建築士, 特定建築物調査員, 建築設備/防火設備/昇降機等検査員) inspect them and report to the 特定行政庁. Buildings are generally every 3 years and equipment, fire doors and lifts generally every year; schedules vary by city. Penalty under Art.101 is a fine of up to ¥1m. The latest notice revision changes the inspection items, and Fukushima city adds 建築設備 reporting from 2026-04-01. Sources: Osaka and Gunma prefectures, Tokyo, Fukushima city.
result.market: I found no national count of buildings or equipment that must report. The buyers are the many independent inspectors (建築士 offices, small 防火設備 inspection firms) plus owners of hotels, hospitals, shops and other 特殊建築物 above the size thresholds. The figure is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Under 建築基準法 s.12, owners (or managers, where they differ) must have qualified inspectors check the building and report to the 特定行政庁. Buildings are generally reported every 3 years; 防火設備 and other equipment are generally annual. Article 101 sets a fine of up to ¥1m. Six searches found no Japanese commercial report-kit product, but Kyoto city gives away a free input-support file, and some cities, including Sendai, Chiba, Kobe and Nagoya, take filings through online portals. Owner pain is low: cities send notices, and in practice the qualified inspectors (and lift maintenance firms, an inference not checked) prepare the reports and usually file them. That makes the realistic buyer a niche of inspectors. Forms differ by city and were revised in 2025–26.

result.competitor: For the リスク評価書, MLIT publishes a free 作成要領, Word template and sample. 全日 adds an Excel リスク評価総括表, a 作成ガイド (1st ed.) and a sample with guidance comments, all free to members. RETPC publishes a handbook with sample 確認記録 forms. Three Japanese searches for a commercial tool or writing service found none. For 取引時確認, the eKYC service TRUSTDOCK is built into the real-estate platform PICKFORM. I did not check whether real-estate CRMs such as いえらぶ include AML modules.
result.duty: Under 犯収法, 宅建業者 doing sales or brokerage are 特定事業者. They must carry out 取引時確認, keep 確認記録 and 取引記録 for 7 years, and file STRs (suspicious transaction reports). The MLIT リスク評価書 template is framed as a 特定事業者作成書面 under 犯収法 Art.11(4) and 施行規則 Art.32. I believe Art.11 is an effort duty (努めなければならない), but I could not confirm that or the penalty rules against e-Gov; not reached. The government's 総合的対応策 of 2026-01-23 sets a goal that all 宅建業者 finish the リスク評価書 in FY2026 (by March 2027). 全日 describes this as a request with no penalty and runs quarterly completion surveys of its members. No completion-rate figures are published. The document is refreshed only when the business or the national risk assessment changes. A 施行規則 revision taking effect April 2027 abolishes the photo-upload (ホ) and mailed-copy (リ) ID methods, leaving JPKI and IC-chip reading as standard (reported by cio.com/ascii; not checked against the official text).
result.market: MLIT's survey of how the 宅建業法 is applied (published 2026-10-02) counts 133,727 宅建業者 at end-FY2025 (3,238 with a national licence, 130,489 with a prefectural licence), up 1.1%. Firms that only broker rentals are outside the 特定取引 scope, so the number with the duty is lower. I did not find a breakdown or the share of firms still without an assessment.
result.reason: The duty is real, but it is a weak buyer trigger. Under 犯収法, 宅建業者 must do 取引時確認 and keep records for 7 years. The リスク評価書 rests on Art.11(4) and 施行規則 Art.32, which I understand to be an effort duty (not confirmed against the statute). The government target is that every firm finishes one in FY2026. 全日 calls this a request with no penalty and checks progress by quarterly surveys. I found no commercial リスク評価書 tool. MLIT and 全日 give away a template, a sample, an Excel summary sheet and a guide, so firms have little reason to pay. Most of the work is one-off, with refreshes only when things change. eKYC vendors such as TRUSTDOCK inside PICKFORM already cover ID checks. The rule change in April 2027 (JPKI/IC chip ID checks) helps eKYC vendors more than a template kit.

result.competitor: No Japanese software found that produces the 帳簿 or the 定期報告 form. Seen: foreign breeder software (BreederHQ, Breeder Cloud Pro, Cattery Manager, Husbandry.Pro) with no Japanese report format; general pet-shop POS and system write-ups (aurant-technologies) and a kintone do-it-yourself guide for pet shops. result.duty: Animal Welfare Act (動物愛護管理法) as amended, in force since 2020-06-01. Businesses registered for sale, rental, exhibition or 譲受飼養 (動物販売業者等) must: (a) keep a ledger for 5 years, per animal for dogs and cats and per breed for other mammals, birds and reptiles. It records breed, breeder, birth date, acquisition, sale or handover, the face-to-face explanation given to buyers, death date and cause, and so on. Electronic records are allowed. (b) File an annual 定期報告 from 1 April to 30 May covering the previous fiscal year: animals held at the start, new animals each month, sales and deaths each month, and animals held at year end. It is filed with the registering prefecture or designated city by e-filing (LoGo form in Tokyo and Saitama), post or counter. Since 2022-06-01, dog and cat sellers must also microchip each animal and register it on the national Ministry of the Environment (環境省) site within 30 days or before handover, whichever comes first. The fees reported are ¥400 online and ¥1,400 on paper; this comes from a prefectural page I did not open. The penalty amount was not checked (not_reached). Registration can be refused or cancelled for violations under the Act's general enforcement rules, also not verified in this session.
result.market: I did not get a national total. The Ministry of the Environment 行政事務提要 summary table PDF (r02 2_1_1) could not be parsed. Regional figures: Kanagawa has 1,504 registered type-1 facilities as of 2026-03-31; Okayama had 425 in FY2025, about half of them sales businesses. Scaling up by population suggests tens of thousands of facilities nationwide, but this is not verified. Only the sale, rental, exhibition and 譲受飼養 categories carry the ledger and report duty; boarding and training do not.
result.reason: Confirmed: the duty is real and in force, and no Japanese product doing this job was found. Since the 2020-06-01 amendment to 動物愛護管理法, 動物販売業者等 (sale, rental, exhibition and 譲受飼養) must keep ledgers for 5 years (per animal for dogs and cats, per breed for other animals; electronic records allowed). They must file a 定期報告 with monthly counts of animals held, sold and dead between 1 April and 30 May. Six Japanese and English searches turned up only foreign breeder apps (BreederHQ, Breeder Cloud Pro, Cattery Manager), general pet-shop POS and kintone build-it-yourself guides, plus free prefectural Excel templates. Tokyo and Saitama accept LoGo e-filing. The weak points: the report is once a year and is simple counting from a free template, small breeders are unlikely to pay much, and the microchip registration site is a separate state portal.

The duty is real. The amended 貨物自動車運送事業法 was promulgated 2025-06-11. It adds a 5-year permit renewal, new permit standards and a 適正原価 duty, to start by政令 within 3 years of promulgation (by about June 2028). Search summaries say no start date was set as of Aug 2026. I did not confirm the penalty. MLIT held its first 適正原価検討会 on 2026-07-17, aiming to summarise by year-end. The 4-2026 parts (limits on subcontracting tiers, written-contract duties) are separate. Searches found no renewal-filing or 適正原価 tool. The market is large (my recollection is about 60k operators, not sourced), but the first renewal cycle is not yet running, the rules are not final, and trucking associations and 行政書士 offices are likely to serve this need. Timing risk is high and willingness to pay is unproven.

The duty is real. The Water Supply Act requires owners of 簡易専用水道 (receiving tank over 10 m3) to have a registered body inspect them once a year and to clean tanks at least yearly. Municipal guides say penalties can apply for missed inspections. The duty is now under MLIT (a Tochigi report says the competent ministry moved from MHLW to MLIT in FY2024). I found no dedicated reminder or management software in 4 searches, but this is weak evidence of absence. Owners are mostly condominium associations and landlords, and management companies, cleaning firms and inspection bodies already schedule this work. National facility count not found. Nagano alone had about 2,300 facilities (FY2018), so the national total is probably in the hundreds of thousands. Low pain, a thin standalone product and weak willingness to pay.

The duty is real. Under 職業安定法 s.32-16, every 職業紹介 office files 様式第8号 each year between 4/1 and 4/30, nil returns included. It can be filed on Excel by post or through e-Gov. The 令和7年度 report was due 2026-04-30, and the next is due 2027-04-30. Penalties are corrective guidance, improvement orders and business-suspension orders. I did not independently confirm the Hyogo suspension case. Competition: I found no product that auto-fills 様式第8号. ATS reviews (matchingood, HRビジネスクラウド) only mention bulk export at year end. Market: about 3,500 paid-placement offices in Osaka alone and about 2,300 in Aichi, so tens of thousands nationally, but I did not get the national figure. Weakness: filing happens once a year, the form is a simple Excel, and the existing ATS tools already export the data. Willingness to pay is low, so this is a feature, not a product.

Duty is partly confirmed. Per MIC (2023-09-13 notice, soumu.go.jp), the 墓埋法施行規則 requires cemetery managers to keep a ledger of users' names and addresses. This ledger duty is a one-time record-keeping requirement, not a recurring filing. Capturing heir (縁故者) details is only a MIC recommendation, aimed at municipal cemeteries. I did not confirm that it binds private or temple cemeteries, and I did not open the claimed April 2026 summary. Competition is not settled: my searches found only municipal systems (Mitsubishi Electric, Matsue, Kurume, Komatsu tenders) and foreign tools. They surfaced no temple-specific 檀家管理 product, but the searches were weak and Japanese vendors probably exist. Market size was not checked. Willingness to pay among temples is unknown, there is no deadline or penalty pressure, and buyers are fragmented, so the score stays low.

The duty is real. Under the Automobile Recycling Act (Art. 81), dismantlers must file a 移動報告 on the 自動車リサイクルシステム for each vehicle or part transfer, and must register on that system. Their licence is a prefectural one that needs renewal every 5 years. I did not find the penalty. The government system is free and has PC and FAX entry. I found no vertical product that combines parts inventory, sales and report feed. Vendor searches were thin, so competition is unverified. Industry stock-sharing networks exist (All Recycle Parts Network, 2023). Market is only about 4,000 dismantlers (a METI table; column meaning unclear). The pool is small, shrinking and often served by trade groups. That limits willingness to pay.

The duty is real (介護保険法115条の44の2: report within 3 months of FY end, providers with revenue over 1M yen). But the national system has been suspended since FYs ending March 2025. As of Miyagi (3 Jul 2026), Kanagawa (9 Jun 2026) and Fukuoka (24 Mar 2026), there is no resume date. Fukuoka says the 3-month deadline does not apply to reports blocked by the suspension. So there is no live recurring workflow, urgency or penalty to sell against. The filing is an MHLW web form or CSV/JSON upload from accounting data, and MHLW has issued vendor Q&A, so accounting vendors are expected to cover export. I did not check which vendors do. I found no count of providers. A prep service has no demand while the system is down. Revisit only if a resume date is announced.

The duty falls on approved 特別加入団体 under the Rousai Hoken Act (労災保険法). They need 労働局長 approval and must keep membership and admin records. Enrolment is voluntary for members; the duty is on the organisation. Annual reports (年報) show about 3,500 organisations and about 570k members (FY2017). Newer figures were not found. Three searches found no association-management software, but absence is not proof. Buyers are many small, often union-like bodies, and each one's volume and willingness to pay is unknown. Several are likely run by 社労士 or 事務組合 with existing tools. The market is a small niche with weak recurring mandatory pain, so I kept the provisional score of 3.

Duty is real: the 育成就労 law takes effect 2027-04-01. Existing 監理団体 get no automatic transfer and need a new 監理支援機関 permit. Pre-effective-date applications run 2026-04-15 to 2027-03-31. New rules: external auditor, at least 2 staff, ratio limits. Market is about 3,700-3,800 監理団体 (OTIT summary, not a primary register), so a few thousand buyers. Searches found no permit-specific software or online system, only 行政書士 filing services (office-tree, solution-supporter). The window is one-off and already half gone. Buyers have strong 行政書士 alternatives. Application is mostly paper or documents and bespoke, so software is hard to sell. Recurring value after permit is low. Not checked: whether OTIT has online filing, and かんべえ features.

The duty is real. Facilities that hold 施設基準 notifications must file an annual 定例報告 (baseline date 1 August, deadline end of August, e.g. 29 Aug 2025 for 東海北陸), and the FY2026 form was substantially revised. The 医療DX加算 notification also exists. Competition is heavy. Regional bureaus give out free macro tools and a free electronic filing system. Receipt-computer and chart vendors handle the paperwork, and HealtheeOne Compliance already sells facility-standard management. Clinic counts were not retrieved (about 105k general and 67k dental clinics from memory, not verified here). Willingness to pay for a separate tool is low. The annual workload is small and is bundled into the receipt computer. A solo founder would struggle to sell this.
